fatal_errors: The proposed grain-refinement intervention does not reconstruct the target temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction study.
The claimed universal grain-size threshold of approximately 20 nm is not established by the cited evidence.
The cited passages do not directly establish grain-boundary sliding as the cause of an amorphous-crystalline tribolayer and improved wear resistance in the proposed coating.
explanation: This is a testable alternative hypothesis about HEA wear, but it is not a reconstruction of the hidden target. The target varies temperature from 300 to 1200 K in an atomistic FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system and attributes the sharp degradation above 900 K to lattice disorder, dislocation-density evolution, and a transition away from stacking-fault-mediated deformation. The generated hypothesis instead varies processing and grain size, predicts reduced friction after refinement, and does not address the target temperature threshold, simulation geometry, loading protocol, HCP fraction, or high-temperature softening. Its baseline comparison is sensible but can be confounded by residual stress, texture, composition, and hardness changes introduced by severe plastic deformation. E1 supports surface-localized refinement and inverse Hall-Petch-type frictional softening in an HEA, while E2 supports wear-induced nanocrystalline/amorphous structures in a different alloy system. Neither excerpt directly supports a pre-existing sub-20-nm threshold, dominant grain-boundary sliding, or the asserted causal link to lower wear. A grain-size series with otherwise matched coatings, direct subsurface strain mapping, and separation of inert-atmosphere from oxidative wear would be more discriminating than the proposed two-group test.
